RECOVERY: the pad stands for a real local; the missing statement is an absolute value taken by masking the sign bit. SPELLING IS LOAD-BEARING: writing it through the TU's existing `union FloatBits { f32 value; u32 bits; }` makes MWCC DEAD-STRIP the whole statement (the union local is never read, so the stores vanish and the score gets WORSE - measured real 122 -> 153, and the instruction count fell further below target, 157 -> 154). The form that reproduces the target is the address-taken pointer cast, because taking the address defeats MWCC's dead-store elimination: `f32 d; d = A - B; *(u32*)&d = *(u32*)&d & 0x7FFFFFFF;` - measured real 122 -> 66 with the instruction count landing exactly on target (163/163) and the opcode multiset going IDENTICAL. NOTE the union spelling is still correct where the masked value IS subsequently read (screen_limitation in the same TU uses it that way and is fine); this law is specifically about the DEAD case, which is the one that needs the escaping address. Shrink the standing pad by the recovered local's size (here `u8 unused[16]` -> `u8 unused[12]`) to hold the frame.
